sentence: AUTO-STD and HOME-PLUS use flat rates; TERM-20 uses a 15% flat default; WL-PAR and FIA-7 use tier schedules.
spec: p1 §2 and p2 §4: product names, lines and flat/tiered bases match; AUTO/HOME are outside scan scope

sentence: Agents have ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, or TERMINATED status, with ACTIVE as the default.
Agent codes and licences and policy numbers are unique, and policy, rate, split, and ledger references must identify existing records.
Policy premium must be positive and is stored to cents; policies default to IN_FORCE and may also be LAPSED or CANCELLED.
Commission rates must be non-null, greater than zero, and at most 50%.
A new rate requires a known product; a named agent must exist and be ACTIVE, while a null agent sets the product default.
Correcting an open rate on its original start date keeps its ID and replaces its percentage and author.
A later new rate closes the earlier open rate for the same product and agent one day before the new start, preserving history and other scopes.
Each product and agent scope has at most one open rate; an end date cannot precede its start, and backdating before the open start is rejected rather than rewriting history.
Ending a rate closes its open scope without deleting history; no open rate raises -20007, and an explicit end date is inclusive.
Splits require a known policy and at least one allocation; replacing splits is permitted even on a lapsed or cancelled policy.
spec: p2 §4.3: every sharing agent must have a split; policy-state restriction not specified

sentence: An agent may appear only once in a policy allocation; null or duplicate agents are rejected.
Each split must be greater than zero and at most 100%, and every allocated agent must exist and be ACTIVE.
Split percentages must sum to exactly 100, with no tolerance; valid allocations replace all prior allocations atomically.
An agent-specific in-force rate wins over the product default; otherwise the default applies, with both date endpoints included.
If several historical rates qualify, the latest start wins within the agent-specific or default scope; absence of a rate raises -20007.
A product is treated as tiered whenever any tier-schedule row exists, not because of its line of business.
For payment, annual premium below $50,000 is T1 and premium of $50,000 or more is T2.
spec: p1 §3 agrees with OLTP; warehouse disagrees at exactly 50000 (CP-045)
decision: D1: Approve T2 at exactly 50000 and align reporting, or choose another shared boundary. OLTP matches the scan; DW labels T1.

sentence: Payment recalculates the tier from the policy’s current premium on every run rather than freezing the issue-time tier.
spec: p1 §3: tier fixed at issue and does not change on premium adjustment
decision: D2: Choose immutable issue premium/tier or approve current-premium repricing; decide how historical recalculation should work.

sentence: WL-PAR T1 uses 45% before the July 2025 change and 40% afterward; WL-PAR T2 uses 30%, FIA-7 T1 6%, and FIA-7 T2 4.5%.
spec: p2 §4 schedule: all numeric rates match; activation date discrepancy is CP-021

sentence: A tier-rate change applies only after its change date, so a policy issued on the change date uses the previous rate or fails if no earlier rate exists.
spec: p2 §4.1: new rate applies on its effective date
decision: D3: Choose inclusive activation from the scan or approve strictly-after-date legacy behavior, including the initial-date no-rate error.

sentence: Tiered payments use the schedule rate selected by policy issue date, overriding any agent-specific flat percentage, but still require a flat rate to exist at period end.
spec: p2 §4.1: issue-date tier-rate basis matches; extra flat-rate dependency not described

sentence: Commission calculation requires an existing IN_FORCE policy and at least one saved split allocation.
Flat-rate commission uses the rate in force on the last day of the requested payment month.
Each monthly agent amount is annual premium divided by 12, times the rate and split percentages, rounded to cents separately for that agent.
spec: p2 §4.2 matches monthly formula and rounding

sentence: A period rerun replaces only that policy’s COMMISSION rows, keeps CHARGEBACK rows, and writes one row per agent, policy, month, and entry type.
Payment uses saved splits without revalidating their totals or the agents’ current status; later suspension does not stop an already allocated agent’s payment.
The requested commission month is not checked against the policy issue date; an in-force policy can receive commission for an earlier month.
A commission insert is reduced to the remaining $2,500 monthly allowance for that agent across other policies, with a floor of zero.
spec: p2 §5: 2500 per agent/calendar month matches initial inserts; lifecycle weaknesses are CP-031

sentence: Chargebacks neither consume nor restore the monthly commission allowance, and unpaid excess is not carried into the next month.
spec: p2 §5: no carry-forward matches; treatment of chargebacks against the cap is not explicit

sentence: The cap is applied in calculation order and only on inserts; lowering a prior policy does not top up other policies, and direct ledger updates can exceed $2,500.
spec: p2 §5: absolute monthly limit across all policies
decision: D4: Decide allocation/recalculation order and whether all write paths must enforce the cap. Current insert-only cap leaves underpayments after repricing and permits over-cap updates; concurrent sessions are not serialized (not load-tested). INSERT SELECT also fails with -4091; choose whether bulk writes must be supported (CP-065).

sentence: Lapse requires a known IN_FORCE policy, changes its status to LAPSED, and rejects a second lapse.
A lapse with fewer than 12 Oracle MONTHS_BETWEEN issue and lapse reverses 100% of all stored commission; at 12 months or later it reverses nothing.
decision: D5: Choose the spec’s 100%/50%/0% bands or legacy 100% before 12 elapsed months, then define policy-month numbering and the anniversary boundary.

sentence: Chargeback is booked in the supplied lapse month per original paid agent, using the negative sum of that agent’s paid commissions and maximum historical rate ID and split percentage.
spec: p3 §6.2: lapse-month booking and paid-agent proportions match if supplied date is processing month

sentence: Lapse chargebacks sum every COMMISSION period on the policy, including periods after the supplied lapse date, and do not validate lapse-date chronology.
spec: p3 §6.1 describes months policy was in force; p3 §6.2 says month lapse is processed
decision: D6: Define chronology, paid-as-of cutoff, and processing-date versus effective-date booking; legacy accepts pre-issue dates and includes future-period ledger amounts.

sentence: There is no surrender operation or SURRENDERED policy state; cancelling a policy does not automatically produce a chargeback.
spec: p3 §6.1 explicitly includes lapse OR surrender
decision: D7: Define surrender representation and whether it must share lapse chargeback behavior. Do not assume CANCELLED means surrendered.

sentence: Successful rate, split, calculation, and lapse operations record the action, actor, detail, and timestamp in the audit log.
Management operations commit on success and roll back the whole current transaction on failure, including changes made by the caller before the call.
A failed commission rerun restores the deleted prior rows and leaves no new calculation audit event.
Tier codes are restricted to T1/T2, and each product/tier/change-date combination may occur only once with a rate in (0,50].
The warehouse refreshes existing agent and product descriptions and inserts missing dimensions from all source records, including inactive agents.
The warehouse creates distinct year, month, and ceiling(month/3) quarter dimensions from ledger months; a null period loads all periods.
Warehouse facts copy the paid ledger amounts, splits, premium, and entry type; ETL does not recompute monetary commission or apply the cap again.
An ETL rerun updates facts by policy, agent, period, and entry type without duplicating them; the returned row count includes matched rows.
The warehouse labels current premiums from zero through $50,000 inclusive as T1, so exactly $50,000 disagrees with the payment package’s T2.
spec: p1 §3: 50000 belongs to T2, agreeing with OLTP not DW
decision: D1: Same boundary decision as CP-018; do not approve the reporting tier just because monetary totals reconcile.

sentence: The warehouse reconstructs tiers from current policy data instead of copying ledger tiers, including assigning tiers to chargebacks whose ledger tier is null.
spec: p1 §3: immutable issue tier; DW derives current tier independently of ledger
decision: D2: Same issue-time snapshot decision as CP-019; decide whether reporting tiers should copy paid-event history, including chargebacks.

sentence: Warehouse loads do not delete facts or dimensions that disappear from the source, so removed allocations can leave stale facts and overstated totals.
decision: D8: Decide whether warehouse is a paid-event archive or a current-ledger mirror; MERGE-only loads retain removed rows. The paired CP-048/049 tests demonstrate the divergence. Also decide how corrected product keys propagate: an existing fact keeps its original product attribution (CP-063).

sentence: A policy’s saved allocation can be removed and the next successful calculation replaces its old-agent ledger rows, leaving no old-agent source row.
After an agent allocation changes, ETL adds the new fact but keeps the deleted agent’s old fact, making reporting differ from the payment ledger.
decision: D8: Same mirror-versus-archive decision as CP-047; monetary reconciliation fails after allocation removal.

sentence: The reporting summary counts fact rows, not distinct policies, and sums signed commission amounts by agent, month, and line of business.
The summary is refreshed only on demand; loading facts alone does not refresh it.
A new tier change dated in the future still makes a product tiered today, but missing earlier schedule coverage stops calculation with -20007.
Premium is taken directly from the annual_premium field for every product; no separate planned-premium or FIA single-premium conversion exists in the database.
spec: p1 §2: planned annual premium, with FIA single premium treated as annualized; database consumes annual_premium only, upstream meaning not verifiable
decision: D9: Confirm career-agency scope and that upstream annual_premium represents planned annualized premium and FIA single premium. The fixture has no channel field or ingestion mapping to prove those assumptions.

sentence: Product lines are restricted to AUTO, HOME, LIFE, ANNUITY, and COMMERCIAL.
Ledger entries permit only COMMISSION or CHARGEBACK and default to COMMISSION; each is unique per policy, agent, and month.
A non-null actor is required by rate-author and audit fields; missing actor causes failure and rolls back the management action.
An explicitly null rate end date leaves the rate open but still records a successful RATE_END audit action.
A lapse with no commission paid still changes status and logs the action but creates no chargeback rows.
spec: p3 §6: only commission already paid is charged back

sentence: Tiered commissions have no first-year or renewal eligibility cutoff; an in-force policy can still be paid the issue-date schedule percentage in later years.
spec: p1 §3 calls these first-year rates; no later-year schedule or payment eligibility is defined
decision: D10: Confirm whether the first-year rate may be paid beyond the first year, or provide renewal eligibility/rates. Code has no duration cutoff; the scan is incomplete for later years.

sentence: Split totals are checked before storage rounding, so three accepted high-precision percentages can persist as a total of 100.01%.
decision: D11: Choose allowed input precision and whether totals must be validated after cent-percentage rounding. Legacy accepts exact input totals that round to a stored total above 100%.

sentence: The commission month is parsed using Oracle’s permissive YYYY-MM conversion and stored as supplied rather than normalized to a canonical month string. Different accepted spellings of the same calendar month use separate cap buckets.
spec: p2 §5: calendar-month agent limit of 2500, regardless of month-string spelling
decision: D4: Same monthly-limit decision as CP-031; require a canonical month key or approve separate legacy string buckets. Tests demonstrate 3000 for the same calendar month.

sentence: Recalculation uses the policy’s current product as well as current premium and allocation, rather than an immutable issue snapshot.
An existing warehouse fact’s product key is not updated when the policy product changes, even though its money is updated from the new product calculation.
decision: D8: Same mirror-versus-archive decision as CP-047; define whether corrected product attribution must propagate to existing facts.

sentence: The rate index permits at most one closed rate per product/agent scope as well as one open rate, so a second supersession or ending after supersession fails and rolls back.
spec: Not addressed by scan for flat-rate history; package documentation promises effective-dated history without deletion
decision: D12: Decide whether arbitrary rate history must be supported. The conditional unique index also restricts closed history, preventing a second historical closure. Do not weaken or replace it without approval.

sentence: Bulk INSERT…SELECT ledger writes fail with Oracle mutating-table error -4091 because the row-level cap trigger queries the same ledger table.
decision: D4: Same cap/write-path decision as CP-031; approve supported write paths and whether bulk ledger operations must be possible.
